lc_person: James Stewart (James S.; Jim) Pritchard (1939–2015), Queen's University history professor; author of Anatomy of a naval disaster and works on naval and New France history.
item_person: Jimmy Stewart / James Franklin Stewart, baseball player (1939–2012); the item also contains conflated authority identifiers and a second death year, 2015.

evidence.says: LC heading is Pritchard, James S., 1939-2015. Source notes identify James Stewart Pritchard, professor emeritus of history at Queen's University, and cite Ships, men, and commerce (1971), Anatomy of a naval disaster (1995), and Elusive empire (2003).

English label is Jimmy Stewart; description and occupation identify a baseball player, and the English Wikipedia sitelink is Jimmy Stewart (baseball). Claims include birth year 1939, death years 2012 and 2015, baseball identifier s/stewaji01, and P244 n87148937, VIAF 12335360 and ISNI 0000000110384907, the historian's authority identifiers.
The graph’s Open Library author identifier resolves to James S. Pritchard, birth year 1939.
Works include Anatomy of a naval disaster (1995), Louis XV’s navy, 1748-1762 (1987), In search of empire (2004), and A bridge of ships. The exact Anatomy title and year match LC’s source note.
The Queen's retirees’ June 2015 newsletter, page 3, lists James Stewart Pritchard in its memorial section with years 1939–2015, independently supporting the LC person's birth year.

notes: Q6201358 conflates the baseball player with the historian; matching birth years and authority identifiers do not establish identity. LC itself links to this same incorrect item. No separate Wikidata item for the historian was found in searches for James Pritchard, James S. Pritchard, James Stewart Pritchard or Jim Pritchard; replacement QID remains unknown.
